children.heading: Program
children.text: The term “program” means the Conserve by Bicycling Program established by subsection (b).

children.heading: Secretary
children.text: The term “Secretary” means the Secretary of Transportation.

tree.heading: Establishment
tree.text: There is established within the Department of Transportation a program to be known as the “Conserve by Bicycling Program”.

children.heading: In general
children.text: In carrying out the program, the Secretary shall establish not more than 10 pilot projects that are—
dispersed geographically throughout the United States; and
designed to conserve energy resources by encouraging the use of bicycles in place of motor vehicles.

children.heading: Requirements
children.text: A pilot project described in paragraph (1) shall—
use education and marketing to convert motor vehicle trips to bicycle trips;
document project results and energy savings (in estimated units of energy conserved);
facilitate partnerships among interested parties in at least 2 of the fields of—
transportation;
law enforcement;
education;
public health;
environment; and
energy;
maximize bicycle facility investments;
demonstrate methods that may be used in other regions of the United States; and
facilitate the continuation of ongoing programs that are sustained by local resources.

children.heading: Cost sharing
children.text: At least 20 percent of the cost of each pilot project described in paragraph (1) shall be provided from non-Federal sources.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Not later than 2 years after August 8, 2005, the Secretary shall enter into a contract with the National Academy of Sciences for, and the National Academy of Sciences shall conduct and submit to Congress a report on, a study on the feasibility of converting motor vehicle trips to bicycle trips.

children.heading: Components
children.text: The study shall—
document the results or progress of the pilot projects under subsection (c);
determine the type and duration of motor vehicle trips that people in the United States may feasibly make by bicycle, taking into consideration factors such as—
weather;
land use and traffic patterns;
the carrying capacity of bicycles; and
bicycle infrastructure;
determine any energy savings that would result from the conversion of motor vehicle trips to bicycle trips;
include a cost-benefit analysis of bicycle infrastructure investments; and
include a description of any factors that would encourage more motor vehicle trips to be replaced with bicycle trips.

tree.heading: Authorization of appropriations
tree.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $6,200,000, to remain available until expended, of which—

children.text: $5,150,000 shall be used to carry out pilot projects described in subsection (c);
$300,000 shall be used by the Secretary to coordinate, publicize, and disseminate the results of the program; and
$750,000 shall be used to carry out subsection (d).
